beats.name: hook
beats.said: The West's top gunslinger lived by one rule: never be the one who draws first.
beats.shown: Smirking red-shirt gunslinger aims a huge revolver; muzzle flash dissolves into a bullet-cam flight down the street to tiny Eddie, ending on a macro of his holster and star buckle.

beats.name: setup
beats.said: At noon you face a calm man called Slow Eddie, who politely lets you go first.
beats.shown: Wide noon street with Eddie far away, holster close-ups, then Eddie in medium close-up with a bored stare and straw; his mouth opens and he nods on the quoted line.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: You snatch your gun faster than ever, yet you're flat on the ground before it's even out.
beats.shown: Challenger panics with wide eyes, sweat and gold flame wisps; camera slams into his holster, tilts to his face; he tumbles, hat flying, and lands face-down in the dirt with dizzy eyes.

beats.name: twist
beats.said: Oddly, Eddie isn't quick at all; a man carrying two drinks would beat him to the saloon.
beats.shown: Dizzy head dissolves to Eddie at a saloon front while a man with two beer mugs gets ahead of him.

beats.name: escalation
beats.said: Challengers come from distant states and all lose alike; the only oddity is Eddie watching their hands.
beats.shown: Golden-hour riders charge through dust; beaten men lie on the ground; at a PHOTOGRAPHS shop a goofy tongue-out loser stands beside Eddie, then a close-up of the two men and their gun hands.

beats.name: explainer
beats.said: Think of catching a falling phone: you grab it before deciding to, because your body reacts automatically.
beats.shown: Dim saloon: the red-shirted man at a card table, a phone slides off the edge and he snatches it; ends on an extreme close-up of his wide eyes.

beats.name: payoff
beats.said: Drawing a gun means choosing the exact moment, and that small decision slows your hand.
beats.shown: Pupil morphs into a round window on the noon street; teal office where a clerk in a green eyeshade works a desk gadget under a THINK BEFORE YOU DRAW sign, windows replaying a fall.

beats.name: ending
beats.said: Eddie makes no decisions; he lets his reflexes answer once your hand moves.
beats.shown: Office turns cold blue with an empty desk; night street standoff: small flash at the challenger's belt, smoke at Eddie's holster, challenger's gun drops.

hook.first_frame: Full-body red-shirted gunslinger in a black hat smirks and aims an oversized revolver at frame right on a sunlit sand street; blurred gun-shop front, blue sky, caption low centre.
hook.first_3s: Smirk turns to gritted teeth (0.2-0.6 s); gun fires through an 8-frame dissolve at 0.77 s; bullet-cam with zoom blur flies down the street to tiny Eddie (2.2 s), who rushes up to a holster macro by 3.0 s.
hook.title_vs_first_line: Title states the answer (second draw wins); the first line states the paradoxical rule (never draw first): the same idea inverted, so the title teases the solution to the opening puzzle.

story.real_fact_core: Reacting to a seen movement is faster than starting a self-chosen one, so the man who waits and reacts can win (reaction versus decision time; Bohr gunfight idea, estimate).

tone.humour: Light slapstick and absurd gags: the fastest gun nicknamed Slow, a beer-carrier race joke, dizzy-eyed face-plant, tongue-out loser.
tone.deadpan_or_irony: Eddie's bored half-lidded stare and calm 'after you' are deadpan; irony that the slow-looking man always wins; narrator stays matter-of-fact.
tone.dialogue_style: Narrator-led second person in short declarative sentences; a single quoted line from Eddie; no back-and-forth.

character_style.outline: Thick uniform-weight black ink outline on heads, torsos and limbs (about 1% of frame width in close shots, estimate); none on the 3D set.
character_style.shading: Flat fills with soft gradient shading (lavender shade on pale heads, warm rim light on edges, glossy gun highlights); faces drawn flat; long soft blue cast shadows at golden hour (estimate).
character_style.consistency_between_shots: Costume, hat, holster and proportions are identical in every shot; face parts (moustache, freckles, eyes, mouth) change per pose (estimate).

animation.body_motion: Rigged 2D puppet parts (head, torso, arms, hat, gun) posed pose-to-pose; falls throw hat, gun and head as separate pieces; some moves repeat in frame pairs (f1212=f1213); FX sprites on extreme poses (estimate).
animation.eyes_and_blinks: Flat drawn eye parts (ring with dot pupil, or half-lidded dash); pupils jump between poses (f940-f1020); no blink frames seen in the sampled holds (estimate).
animation.idle_motion: Eddie is near-frozen in holds (no visible breathing; only a nod and hat tilt); the other man waves his arms and swaps faces; slow camera push-ins supply most motion (estimate).
animation.squash_and_stretch: Little: rigid capsule bodies; head scales up and tilts as he lands (f508-f544); Eddie's hat tilts on the nod (f358); no volume-preserving squash seen (estimate).

generation_evidence.observation: PHOTOGRAPHS sign and its tiny subtext keep identical spelling and shape across a 3.4 s push-in while defocused; no letter warping.
FIRST BANK sign, windows and cornice keep rigid perspective-correct geometry on a static camera; characters repeat the same costume details.
Flame wisps, glow ring and speed lines are flat 2D sprites over a 3D-lit blurred street; hat and holster shapes stay identical frame to frame.
Hat, gun, head and body move as separate objects with clean ballistic arcs and dust sprites; head size changes between poses by design, not by drift.
During a fast camera orbit frames come in identical pairs (1212=1213, 1214=1215): a held-frame cadence typical of keyed or on-twos output (estimate).
Eddie's mouth swaps between a closed moustache and an open-mouth sprite while outline weight, hat and straw stay constant; no morphing or drifting detail.
